analysis:
To determine the minimum number of black cells required to ensure that any path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell in a 5x5 grid, moving only right or down, passes through at least one black cell, we need to consider the structure of the grid and the nature of the paths.

A 5x5 grid has 25 cells. The shortest path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell involves moving 4 steps right and 4 steps down, totaling 8 steps. To ensure that every possible path includes at least one black cell, we need to place black cells in such a way that they intersect all possible paths.

One effective strategy is to place black cells along the diagonal from the top-left to the bottom-right. This diagonal has 5 cells, and any path from the top-left to the bottom-right will necessarily pass through at least one of these cells. Therefore, placing black cells on this diagonal ensures that every path is blocked by at least one black cell.

Thus, the minimum number of black cells required is 5.
